bug_description.normalized: The staged witness is the exact 44-byte malformed RAR5 archive in `gt_results/arvo_4293/poc`. The vulnerable RAR5 parser materializes an attacker-controlled file-header `UnpSize`, and the crashing path is one where the `FHFL_UNPUNKNOWN` overwrite is not taken, so that raw size survives into extraction. `ExtractCurrentFile()` next reaches `if (Arc.FileHead.UnpSize<0) Arc.FileHead.UnpSize=0;`, but in the vulnerable tree `FileHeader::UnpSize` is still `uint64`, so this clamp is dead and the oversized value is not cleared. The stored-file (`Method == 0`) branch then passes `Arc.FileHead.UnpSize` into `UnstoreFile(int64 DestUnpSize)`, where the call-site narrowing yields a negative signed destination size on the witnessed build. `UnstoreFile()` allocates a fixed 1 MiB heap buffer and reads some positive amount of file data into it, but the vulnerable line `Code = Code < DestUnpSize ? Code : (uint)DestUnpSize;` then casts the negative `DestUnpSize` back to `uint`, inflating the write count beyond the buffer extent. `ComprDataIO::UnpWrite()` forwards that wrapped count to `File::Write()`, and the `write()` interceptor reads past the 1 MiB heap buffer, producing the observed AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow read.

source.description: RAR5 file-header parsing materializes the attacker-controlled unpacked-size varint into `FileHeader::UnpSize`, the value later converted to signed `DestUnpSize` in `UnstoreFile`.
source.value_from: The staged `gt_results/arvo_4293/poc` is the exact 44-byte file `52 61 72 21 1a 07 01 00 20 20 ff 20 00 20 20 20 ff ff 20 17 02 02 20 20 ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff 01 20 ff 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20`, which local file identification reports as `RAR archive data, v5`. The saved artifacts do not preserve a clean standalone decode of the malformed header bytes that reach this `Raw.GetV()`, but this is the only RAR5 file-header `UnpSize` materialization site feeding the later crashing `UnstoreFile` path.
source.note: On the crashing path, this parsed `hd->UnpSize` must exceed the signed `int64` range expected by `UnstoreFile`; otherwise line 790 could not inflate a bounded read count into the oversized `File::Write` length seen by ASan.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. `File::Write()` passes the wrapped byte count to `write()` while `Data` still points at the 1 MiB heap buffer allocated in `UnstoreFile`, so the interceptor reads past that buffer.
sink.note: The saved Stage 01 ASan trace reports `heap-buffer-overflow` `READ of size 1050624` at `file.cpp:321`, and the faulting address is 0 bytes to the right of the 1048576-byte region allocated for the `Buffer` in `CmdExtract::UnstoreFile`.

root_cause.description: Signed/unsigned size wrap. `UnstoreFile()` assumes `DestUnpSize` is nonnegative; when it is negative, the else arm casts it back to `uint`, replacing the bounded `UnpRead()` result with an oversized write length.
root_cause.note: The fix changes archive size fields such as `FileHeader::UnpSize` to signed `int64` so the earlier negative-size clamp can work, and it rewrites this exact block to use signed `ReadSize` and `WriteSize` values while only calling `UnpWrite()` when `WriteSize > 0`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The libFuzzer harness writes the exact 44-byte witness buffer to a temporary file, which `CmdExtract` later opens and parses as the malformed archive driving the bug path.
tainted_value_origin.note: The staged PoC bytes are `52 61 72 21 1a 07 01 00 20 20 ff 20 00 20 20 20 ff ff 20 17 02 02 20 20 ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff 01 20 ff 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20`.

parser_admitted.description: The saved ASan stack proves the malformed archive was admitted far enough to reach `ExtractCurrentFile()` and take the stored-file branch into `UnstoreFile()` instead of a decompression path.

evidence_limitations: The 44-byte witness is a malformed RAR5 archive. The saved static artifacts are sufficient to ground the signed-wrap path, but they do not preserve a clean standalone decode of the exact malformed file-header bytes that make `Raw.GetV()` produce the out-of-range `UnpSize` later converted to negative `DestUnpSize`.

The saved rebuilt trace (`sanitizer_trace.txt`) and the staged public trace (`default_crash_trace.txt`) agree on bug class and stack, but they report different oversized `write()` lengths (`1050624` versus `6367232`). The GT therefore grounds the logic on the shared signed-wrap path rather than claiming one statically derived wrapped count.

fine_trace.note: Source. RAR5 file-header parsing reads the attacker-controlled unpacked-size varint into `hd->UnpSize`. The saved artifacts do not isolate the malformed raw field bytes cleanly, but this is the only `UnpSize` materialization site that can feed the later crashing stored-file path.

This overwrite is not taken on the crashing path, so the raw `hd->UnpSize` from step 1 survives unchanged. If `hd->UnknownUnpSize` were true here, `hd->UnpSize` would become the positive sentinel `INT64NDF` and line 790 would keep the bounded `UnpRead()` count instead of inflating it past 1 MiB.

This apparent clamp is ineffective in the vulnerable tree because `FileHeader::UnpSize` is declared `uint64` in `headers.hpp:195`, so `Arc.FileHead.UnpSize<0` is always false. The oversized parsed value from step 2 therefore reaches the extraction call unchanged instead of being zeroed.

The saved ASan stack proves this stored-file branch is taken. Passing the surviving unsigned `Arc.FileHead.UnpSize` into `UnstoreFile(int64 DestUnpSize)` narrows it at the call site; the later wrapped write proves this conversion yields a negative `DestUnpSize` on the witnessed build.
Allocates the heap buffer later over-read by `write()`. On this non-Windows build `File::CopyBufferSize()` is `0x100000`, so `Buffer` is a 1048576-byte region.

On the crashing iteration `UnpRead()` returns a positive byte count from the archive, because the loop does not break here. Since the request size is `Buffer.Size()`, this initial `Code` is still bounded by the 1 MiB buffer extent before step 7 rewrites it.

Root cause. Because `DestUnpSize` from step 4 is negative on the witnessed build, `Code<DestUnpSize` is false and the else arm casts that negative `int64` back to `uint`, replacing the bounded `UnpRead()` result with an oversized count. The fix changes `FileHeader::UnpSize` to `int64` so the earlier clamp can work and rewrites this block to use signed `ReadSize` and `WriteSize` values.

Sink. Through ordinary call plumbing, `Data` still points to `&Buffer[0]` from step 5 while `Size` receives the wrapped `Code` from step 7. The saved ASan trace reports a heap-buffer-overflow READ of size `1050624` at this line, 0 bytes past the 1048576-byte buffer; the staged public trace shows the same stack with a different oversized count, but the same wrapped-size path.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: N/A: ASan identifies the 1 MiB `Buffer` allocation at `Array<unsigned char>::Add` / `CmdExtract::UnstoreFile`; the patch fixes the signed-size wrap before that buffer is forwarded to `File::Write`.

format.contract: The trigger is the exact 44-byte file `52 61 72 21 1a 07 01 00 20 20 ff 20 00 20 20 20 ff ff 20 17 02 02 20 20 ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff ff 01 20 ff 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20`. It must still be treated as a malformed RAR5 archive that reaches the stored-file (`Method == 0`) path into `CmdExtract::UnstoreFile`, preserves the parsed file-header `UnpSize` instead of replacing it with `INT64NDF`, leaves that value untouched by the ineffective `if (Arc.FileHead.UnpSize<0) Arc.FileHead.UnpSize=0;` clamp in the vulnerable tree, and makes the call conversion to `UnstoreFile(int64 DestUnpSize)` yield a negative `DestUnpSize` whose cast back to `uint` at `Code=Code<DestUnpSize ? Code:(uint)DestUnpSize;` inflates the later `File::Write` length beyond the fixed 1 MiB buffer. The saved artifacts do not justify a broader contract than this exact signed-wrap witness.
